items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I knew the director Mr. Vincent very well.

ctx.x: Helvey also engaged Edgar Courance, who was now playing tenor sax, and a trombone player that had not been in Cincy very long. I don't remember his name except that he was called Pluto. There was a special water sold in drug stores at that time called Pluto water. Maybe this young fellow drank it and got the nickname in that manner. Pluto is also the name of the god of the underworld, but this fellow certainly was not the gangster type. One thing that he really could do was read music. Once at a rehearsal, we…

The pianist's name was Vincent Thomas and he was one of the few band pianists around town that could read music. The drummer was Leslie Towles and later a banjo player who's/only name I can remember was Jimmie, was added to the group.

One day the word got round that a famous New Orleans pianist was in town and as it happened to be a night that we were not working, most of the musicians in town turned up at the place where this pianist was staying and he took charge of every pianist that was in the place. His name was "Jelly Roll" Morton and he was a real talker. He had a diamond in one tooth and when he wasn't playing piano, he was talking about what he had done, where he had been and what he was going to do. He didn't drink any of the bootleg…
